title: Matsyapurana
source: sa_matsyapurANa1-176.txt; GRETIL (gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (data entry: Oliver Hellwig)
reply:
Only a few verses state a kinship relation outright.

- 47.177 says Kāvya (Bhārgava) took Jayantī's hand ("jayantyāḥ pāṇimudvahan"), which makes her his wife. Kāvya is not named in this verse itself, but the subject is carried over from the preceding verses, so I mark it as doubtful.
- 47.185 says Devayānī was born at the end of the ten years ("devayānī tadotpannā"). The verse does not name her parents, so it gives no relation.
- 47.217 says "tava pautraḥ punarbaliḥ", so Bali is the grandson of the person addressed. Verse 47.209 shows Prahlāda addressing Śukra, but the speaker and addressee in 47.217 are Brahmā's words relayed by Śukra to the asuras. The addressee is therefore unclear. 47.206 puts Prahlāda at the front of the asuras, which suggests the addressee is Prahlāda. Because this is an inference, I mark it as doubtful and record Bali as the descendant of Prahlāda.
- 47.218 repeats this: "pautraste viṣṇunā". The verse names no person for "te", so I leave it out.

Verse 47.170 calls Jayantī an "anucarī" of the god, which is a servant relation, not kinship.
